newsitem.title: USA: DuPont had record net on oil, chemicals.
newsitem.headline: DuPont had record net on oil, chemicals.

text.p: DuPont Co Wednesday reported record fourth quarter and full-year 1996 earnings citing excellent petroleum product performance and strong chemicals and specialties volumes in the second half.
Fourth quarter 1996 earnings per share of $1.52 were $0.39 higher than the fourth quarter 1995. Excluding 1995 charges, earnings for the latest quarter were up 19 percent, it said.
Although the results trailed the First Call consensus of $1.54, Bear Stearns upgraded DuPont following the report.
Full year earnings were $6.47 per share compared to $5.61 per share in 1995.
"This was another strong year for DuPont and the third consecutive year of record earnings.

Upstream petroleum results -- from the refining and marketing operations of its Conoco Inc subsidiary -- increased 46 percent to $706 million and were a major contributor to earnings growth, said chief executive John A. Krol.

He said the company has regained financial flexibility by essentially completing repayment of the $8 billion of debt incurred in 1995 to redeem shares from Seagram Co Ltd and by repurchasing for $500 million the 156 million warrants issued to Seagram.
Sales for the fourth quarter were $11.4 billion, up 10 percent from the prior year, DuPont said.
This reflects a 26 percent increase in petroleum sales, principally from higher crude oil and natural gas prices, and a two percent decrease in chemicals and specialties sales.

It said chemicals and specialties sales were up six percent after adjusting for changes in business composition resulting from the divestiture of medical products businesses and forming the DuPont Dow Elastomers joint venture.

This reflected 10 percent growth both inside and outside of the United States. These gains were partly offset by lower worldwide selling prices that averaged four percent below the fourth quarter 1995.
Net income for the quarter was $858 million. DuPont said that's an increase of 21 percent from 1995's final three months excluding nonrecurring items.
In all of 1996, DuPont said, oil production and natural gas deliveries rose six percent and five percent, respectively.
Chemicals and Specialties sales for the year were down four percent, reflecting changes in business composition.

Excluding the effect of these changes on reported sales, Chemicals and Specialties sales were up two percent versus 1995, reflecting three percent higher sales volume, partly offset by one percent lower average selling prices. U.S. prices were flat, while prices outside the United States averaged three percent lower, largely attributable to a stronger U.S. dollar. Outside the United States volume improved four percent, principally from growth in the Asia Pacific region. U.S. sales volume was up almost three percent.
